_meta.title: AI Compute Supply-Side Constraint Parameters
_meta.principle: Four evidence classes: observed = source-reported historical measurement (verification separate); derived = arithmetic; calibrated = chosen using an output target; assumption = judgment, extrapolation or reported forecast. Primary and secondary sources are mixed. Inherited claims are unverified except where explicitly marked.
_meta.units: Capacity in GW of critical IT load unless stated. Lead times in months.
_meta.known_definitional_conflict: North America signed bookings are bridged to US by an assumed share and allocated to requested-service years. CBRE occupancy is context only. Company-wide AI capex is a separate demand lens; these series are never summed.

us_disclosed_pipeline_gw.note: Total disclosed US data center pipeline.

share_under_active_development.note: Inherited pipeline snapshot share. Applying it as a cohort conversion gate is a modeling proxy, not an observed lifetime conversion probability.

sightline_2026_under_construction_gw.note: Implies a 31% announced-to-construction rate for the near-dated cohort, consistent with the Wood Mackenzie 33%.

delay_or_cancel_rate_low.note: Low end of expected 2026 delay/cancellation range.

quarterly_pipeline_additions_q4_2025_gw.note: New pipeline additions in Q4 2025, down 50% from ~50 GW in Q3 2025. Annualises to ~100 GW/yr of fresh announcements. Used as the ongoing announcement FLOW; the 241 GW disclosed figure is the STOCK that flow accumulates into, so the two must not both be fed to the funnel or announcements are double counted.

annual_announcement_flow_gw.source: Derived by annualising Wood Mackenzie Q4 2025 additions
annual_announcement_flow_gw.note: Annual run-rate extrapolation from Q4; not an observed annual flow.

historical_ir_to_cod_completion_rate.note: Share of capacity submitting interconnection requests 2000-2020 that had reached commercial operation by end-2025. The longest-run empirical estimate of announcement-to-delivery conversion available anywhere. Generation-side; used here as the outside view on any queue-dependent pathway.

historical_withdrawal_rate.note: Withdrawn share of the same cohort. Remaining 10% still active.

median_ir_to_cod_years.note: Median for projects reaching COD in 2025; reported as 'over 5 years', so this is a floor.

active_queue_generation_gw.note: Active generation capacity in US queues as of end-2025, across ~8,200 projects.

active_queue_gas_gw.note: Up 86% in 2025 while solar (-19%), storage (-16%) and wind (-19%) contracted. The queue is re-composing toward firm capacity.

large_load_queue_gw.note: More than five times ERCOT's record peak demand.

approval_to_energize_gw.note: Large loads holding Approval to Energize.

observed_peak_large_load_gw.note: Observed peak consumption, not energized capacity. Different dates and populations prevent a queue conversion ratio.

audit_start.source: Gov. Abbott directive; ERCOT postponed Batch Zero classification

audit_target_completion.note: ERCOT has said the Batch Zero study will NOT be complete by its April 9, 2027 deadline and has not yet proposed a replacement date. Treat 2026-12-10 as the audit milestone, not the resumption of study results.

batch_zero_study_slip.note: Inherited reported schedule slip. Context only; no regional shock is implemented.

medium_load_pipeline_mw.source: ERCOT April snapshot via Utility Dive
medium_load_pipeline_mw.note: 157 medium data center and crypto facilities below the Batch Zero threshold.

sb6_financial_security_per_mw_usd.source: PUCT draft rule 16 TAC 25.194 under SB6
sb6_financial_security_per_mw_usd.note: Applies to loads 75 MW+, alongside site control, batch study and mandatory curtailment exposure. Raises real project cost and thins speculative requests.

power_substation_transformer.source: Wood Mackenzie 2026 read via VAWN index
power_substation_transformer.note: Over 160 weeks. Largest HV units reach up to 4 years (48 months).

power_substation_transformer_worst.source: IEA transmission equipment lead times via VAWN

gsu_transformer.source: Wood Mackenzie survey via VAWN / IndustrialSage
gsu_transformer.note: 144 weeks. Generator step-up units above 50 MVA reported at 100-150+ weeks.

mv_switchgear_15kv.note: 52-80 weeks; pre-pandemic comparable was about 24 weeks.

large_frame_gas_turbine.source: Secondwatt synthesis of OEM order books
large_frame_gas_turbine.note: US wait times up to seven years for some frames; large turbines commonly quoted around five. Midpoint 5.5 years used.

aeroderivative_gas_turbine.source: Secondwatt synthesis of OEM order books
aeroderivative_gas_turbine.note: Midpoint of inherited 18–36 month generation lead range. Full route also waits for transformers and other components.

site_build_shell_and_fitout.source: Industry standard data center build cycle
site_build_shell_and_fitout.note: ASSUMPTION. Shell-to-commissioning absent power constraint. Sourced commentary repeatedly references an 18-month build cycle as the baseline that equipment lead times now exceed.

ge_vernova_backlog_gw.note: Up from 100 GW three months earlier and 83 GW at end-2025. Expects 125 GW under contract by December. Taking reservations for 2031 delivery.

siemens_energy_backlog_gw.note: Booked 15 GW and shipped six in the quarter. Lead times three years or more.

industry_annual_capacity_gw_low.note: Against roughly 110 GW of annual orders. Book runs 1.6-1.8 years deep before a new order is reached.

us_share_of_turbine_output.source: Derived from Siemens Energy CEO comment that addressable market could reach 120 GW/yr, roughly half American
us_share_of_turbine_output.note: ASSUMPTION. Applied to allocate global OEM throughput to US deliverability.

data_center_share_of_us_turbine_output.source: Explicit model judgment; no external observation
data_center_share_of_us_turbine_output.note: ASSUMPTION, and a material one. Turbines also serve utility fleet replacement, coal retirement backfill and industrial load. Sensitivity range 0.30-0.60 in scenarios.

na_absorption_h1_2026_gw.source: JLL North America Data Center Report
na_absorption_h1_2026_gw.note: Double year-earlier level, five times H1 2024. INCLUDES hyperscale self-build. Not comparable to CBRE's colo figure.

cbre_primary_supply_mw.source: CBRE North America Data Center Trends H1 2026

cbre_primary_vacancy.note: Down from 1.6% a year earlier. Record low. Third consecutive year near 1%.

cbre_preleased_share_of_construction.note: Reported prelease share; neither proof of future occupancy nor a test of a capex bubble. Context only.

cbre_net_absorption_h1_2026_mw.note: Primary colocation markets only. Do NOT sum with the JLL 25 GW figure.

hyperscaler_2026_capex_usd_bn.source: CreditSights via Global Data Center Hub
hyperscaler_2026_capex_usd_bn.note: Five largest hyperscalers, up 36% YoY, roughly 75% AI-tied.

generation_nameplate_per_gw_it_load.source: Explicit model judgment; no external observation
generation_nameplate_per_gw_it_load.note: ASSUMPTION. Dedicated behind-the-meter generation nameplate required per GW of critical IT load, allowing for availability and maintenance reserve. Sensitivity 1.05-1.35.

aeroderivative_unit_mw_typical.note: Representative aeroderivative unit rating. Campuses in this class are assembled from ~25-30 units to reach roughly 1 GW of nameplate, which is why the pathway scales in increments rather than in single large blocks.

reference_year.note: Fixed origin for forecasts and opening cohorts.

pathway_shares.note: Allocation of mutually exclusive new-build routes; sums to one.

colo_development_gate.note: New merchant colocation development; not leases on existing construction.

colo_power_gate.note: Conditional power conversion; transformers are not assumed secured.

aero_turbine_share.note: Dedicated fraction of turbine capacity. Unused allocation is not transferred across turbine types.

site_permitting_months.note: Parallel elapsed readiness time from announcement.

commissioning_ready_months.note: Total elapsed readiness milestone including shell/fit-out and commissioning; not an extra sequential duration.

opening_announcements_gw.note: Illustrative US backcast, NOT measured historical announcements. Replaces construction-stock seeding entirely. Pending post-2025 deliveries only; earlier deliveries and rationing excluded. Sensitivity required.

landing_rule.note: Annual timing approximation: split fractional lags between adjacent calendar years. Not a project-level delivery-date promise.

opening_equipment_backlog_gw.note: No inherited equipment backlog at the reference year; pre-window volumes landing after reference still enter the queue.

bookings_us_share.note: Illustrative bridge from North America signed bookings to US; not an observed geographic share.

booking_delivery_weights.note: Requested-service lag weights for signed bookings: years 0, 1, 2. Sum to one.

opening_bookings_us_gw.note: Illustrative US bookings signed before the forecast origin. No additional opening demand stock.

opening_sensitivity.note: Multipliers on illustrative opening announcement cohorts.

horizon_years.note: Default reporting horizon; origin stored separately.

h1_annualization_factor.note: Assume H2 equals H1 to initialize signing flow, not delivery-year demand.

quarter_annualization_factor.note: Assume quarterly announcement flow repeats four times.

grid_lifetime_conversion_proxy.note: Transfer of generation queue completion rate to load-side projects is an assumption. Conditional power gate = min(1, proxy / development gate); no independent second 13% haircut.

value.label: US turbine allocation to data centers
US share of North America bookings

ui_controls.note: Exploratory control ranges, not confidence intervals.

supply_topologies.source: Explicit model judgment; alternative topology not externally verified
supply_topologies.note: Component exclusions by pathway. Alternative BTM replaces only the existing aero route; assumes no new HV substation or GSU procurement is needed and other electrical readiness is covered by retained milestones. Does not establish equipment availability or engineering feasibility. All shares, gates, turbine ceilings and opening announcements remain fixed; no additional supply route is added.

cbre_primary_inventory_2025_gw.note: Year-end total inventory across eight primary markets. NOT annual US new delivery; excluded from calibration and accuracy scoring.
